subject: Transportation Systems
title: Wayfinding and Maps
description: A fast breakdown of Wayfinding and Maps for builders.

hook.text: Harry Beck's 1931 London Tube map ignored real geography. It just showed connections. Revolutionary.

buildup.text: He straightened lines, evened out station spacing, and used color coding for each route.

discovery.text: The map was rejected at first—too abstract. Then passengers loved it because it was so easy to read.

twist.text: Every metro map in the world now copies Beck's approach. Geography doesn't matter—connections do.

climax.text: Modern wayfinding adds real-time displays, app navigation, and multilingual signage.

punchline.text: The best transit map is a diagram, not a map.

quiz.question: What made Harry Beck's Tube map revolutionary?
options: It focused on connections instead of geography
